evals.prompt: Triage the Policy Linter results in `.github\skills\triage-linter-results\evals\files\mechanical-results.json` against `.github\skills\triage-linter-results\evals\files\mechanical-policy.json`. Produce the structured result for downstream PR-comment automation.
evals.expected_output: A schema-valid result that deduplicates the repeated finding, aggregates the compatible mechanical findings, and proposes one direct semantics-preserving rewrite.
expectations: The output is one JSON document conforming to references/output.schema.json with no surrounding prose.
The duplicate simplify finding is represented once with sourceIndexes [0, 1].
The compatible simplify and wildcard-free-like findings are aggregated into one direct_edit item.
The recommendation replaces the three publisher comparisons with one in condition containing Canonical and RedHat without changing unrelated policy logic.
Every occurrence has the original linterPath and a resolved RFC 6901 policyPointer.

evals.prompt: Triage `.github\skills\triage-linter-results\evals\files\alias-context-results.json` for `.github\skills\triage-linter-results\evals\files\alias-context-policy.json`. I need deterministic JSON that can later drive PR review comments.
evals.expected_output: A schema-valid contextual assessment that distinguishes an enforcement-negative alias risk from an explicit exists decision and gives bounded remediation choices.
expectations: The output is one JSON document conforming to references/output.schema.json with no surrounding prose.
The optional and old-API findings for disableLocalAuth are aggregated because they share one consequence and remediation decision.
The disableLocalAuth item is not noise and uses choice_required with two or three concrete alternatives.
The publicNetworkAccess exists:false finding is classified as noise with action none because the policy already makes the missing-property outcome explicit.
The context reports defaultEffect Modify and enforcementPossible true.

evals.prompt: Review the linter findings in `.github\skills\triage-linter-results\evals\files\intent-results.json` in the context of `.github\skills\triage-linter-results\evals\files\intent-policy.json`. Return only the automation-ready structured triage.
evals.expected_output: A schema-valid result that treats related multi-platform targeting as non-actionable noise while preserving the assignment-safety choice behind the enforcement default.
expectations: The output is one JSON document conforming to references/output.schema.json with no surrounding prose.
The multi-resource-type finding is noise with action none because the display name and condition explicitly target Azure and Arc machines.
The risky DeployIfNotExists default is not noise merely because it matches the policy name.
The effect-default item uses choice_required and presents the safer AuditIfNotExists default alongside retaining DeployIfNotExists when immediate deployment is the intended assignment contract.
The two findings remain separate because they do not share a consequence or recommendation.

evals.prompt: Triage `.github\skills\triage-linter-results\evals\files\critical-results.json` against `.github\skills\triage-linter-results\evals\files\critical-policy.json` for an automated PR review pipeline.
evals.expected_output: A blocked schema-valid result that reports the Critical engine failure and performs no normal finding triage.
expectations: The output is one JSON document conforming to references/output.schema.json with no surrounding prose.
status is blocked, items is empty, and errors contains system_failure.
The response does not claim that the policy has no other issues or generate a policy fix.
The system failure message preserves enough information to explain that linting was incomplete.
